 DeMar DeRozan takes back historic NBA spot from Stephen Curry 
 2026-11-15 12:04 
 DeMar DeRozan passed Stephen Curry for 16th place on the NBA's all-time scoring list on Saturday, reclaiming the position just five days after the injured Warriors superstar had overtaken him.
 Credit: AP - Scanpix

 Denver Nuggets veteran wing DeMar DeRozan has overtaken Golden State Warriors superstar Stephen Curry on the NBA's all-time scoring list, reclaiming 16th place just five days after Curry had moved ahead of him.
 Player of the Game

 The 37-year-old scored nine points in Denver's 116-108 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday night, bringing his career total to 26,810 points, four more than Curry's 26,806.
 DeRozan played 23 minutes off the bench, shooting 3-of-6 from the field and 3-of-4 from the free-throw line. He also contributed three rebounds and two assists.
 Curry had previously overtaken DeRozan for 16th place on November 9, scoring 25 points in Golden State's 138-87 victory over the Pelicans.
 That performance lifted Curry to 26,803 career points, temporarily moving him ahead of DeRozan in what has become a close race between the two veterans.
 Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix 
 However, Curry is currently sidelined with an oblique abdominal tear, which he suffered during Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets.
 An MRI confirmed the injury, and the Warriors announced that the two-time NBA MVP would be re-evaluated in two weeks .
 Before the injury, the 38-year-old Curry was averaging 27.8 points, 3.9 assists, and 3.7 rebounds over 10 games this season.
 DeRozan and Curry's NBA all-time scoring rankings
 With 26,810 career points, DeRozan now ranks 16th in NBA history, sitting just 136 points behind Hall of Famer Hakeem Olajuwon, who holds 15th place with 26,946.
 Curry, meanwhile, has dropped to 17th, though the two could trade places again once the Warriors superstar returns from injury.
 LeBron James continues to lead the NBA's all-time scoring list with 43,591 regular-season points.
